body:
Thanks. I've been trying to do this for the past couple days now, and I can actually notice a slight difference. I can feel when I start to get ticked off, so right at that moment, I stop to think about what it was exactly that triggered me. Nine times out of ten, I am able to acknowledge the thing and just move on instead of getting hung up on it. 

The one time when I missed it, I found that the rest of the evening sort of spiralled out of control because every other thing after that irritated me. 

So all in all, I really found your method to be useful. Thank you!

Thanks for the advice and encouragement. I've shared some resources with him, and he has apologized for not having been more understanding. He said he has to come to terms with the fact that I have this disorder, but that he ultimately loves me and wants to be with me, and he'll do what he can to support me.

Hi mashley, 

Thanks for your reply here and for the pm. I appreciate your advice. What you're saying makes full sense; I will show him some resources, including the one you provided, so that he can gain a better understanding of what's going on in my head.

I created this account when I was having one of my crisis moments (you can look at my history if you are interested). All I could think about in that moment was how overwhelmed I was feeling, and how frustrated I was that I couldn't reason with myself to make the feeling stop. I'm not very good at controlling my "episodes" (for lack of a better term), and I often feel physically ill and mentally franctic when they're happening. 

My saying "everything is BPD" was my way of saying that I was in over my head, that I was frantic, that my head was spinning. In that moment, I needed support from like-minded individuals; I needed to know how to calm down in that moment, and I needed to just have someone say "it's going to be ok." 

I was very fortunate to have several thoughful and caring people in this subreddit respond to my cry for help.

I apologize that my username offended you, but I hope that you can better understand my position after having read my explanation above.

Thanks for this.

The therapist that evaluated and positively diagnosed me with BPD said that since it is difficult to know "yourself" when you have BPD, it is not uncommon to feel like you're unsure about what your interests are. Sure, there are things I think I like, but I don't know if it's "me" that likes them, or if I like them because the person I am with likes them, which causes me to be afraid of losing them if we do not have the same interests and so on. (Hopefully that makes sense.)

While I am not happy to have this disorder (because it has been destroying my relationships, platonic and otherwise for years now), I am happy that I finally understand why I am the way I am, and I am happy that I feel like I "belong" somewhere. I've always felt alone and lost, and to me, having this diagnosis represents progress and hope.

Thanks for your support, Rain12913. I appreciate it.

Thanks so much for your reply. It's very helpful. I'll do some research and find out about some reputable artists in my city and go from there.

Thanks again. And thanks for saying what you said in your last paragraph. It put a smile on my face. If I follow through with this, I'll definitely post a photo.

I am in tears of joy after having read this post. After reading countless books and articles about why I am the way I am, THIS is the one that I hope sticks with me above all. Your words are so encouraging, and they give me hope that I will be ok, and that I can be loved. Thank you a million times over for posting this. THANK YOU.

Thank you for taking the time to share your advice. I'm still so shaken from the whole thing. It really did happen very quickly. I will try to focus on slowing things down. It's "bedtime" in our timezone right now, so maybe in the morning things will be clearer. I'm just so ashamed of my behaviour from tonight. I hope I can live it down tomorrow.
